answer: Ferrous delay gradient: each new identity must wait through a unique sequence of registration windows derived from its claimed history, so identities created in the same minute cannot proceed together. The system measures arrival spacing per subnet; clusters arriving faster than a copper-threshold rate are throttled into staggered queues. Every identity pays a per-window holding cost, so a burst of N sybils multiplies delay and fee across each terrace of the queue, making mass creation linearly expensive in time and money.
